newsitem.title: USA: Kansas City Southern Q3 rail revs fall.
newsitem.headline: Kansas City Southern Q3 rail revs fall.

text.p: Kansas City Southern Industries Inc said on Wednesday that its railroad revenues fell in the third quarter to $125.5 million from $129.0 million, partly because of mergers in the industry.

"As expected, the various rail mergers have negatively affected KCSR (Kansas City Southern Railway) revenues. However, management's recent operational improvements and cost containment efforts have minimised their impact on earnings," president and chief executive Landon Rowland said.
Third quarter net income from the railway unit rose to $7.2 million from $6.6 million a year ago, the company said.

At the company's financial asset management unit, which includes the Janus and Berger mutual fund families, revenues surged in the third quarter to $85.9 million from $62.8 million a year ago and third quarter net income increased to $18.8 million from $13.8 million.

In a separate statement, Kansas City Southern said it would be working with the Washington Organisation in operating certain portions of Canadian Pacific Ltd's Soo Line in Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota and Missouri.
